proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the bump-function argument), stated for an arbitrary subspace V. Compare Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 and the test-function argument of Remark 1.5(3), book/chapter-03.txt lines 76–91.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For r ∈ ℝ, η_r := blowUpMap x r, so η_r(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x), and S_r := η_r(A) = blowUpMap x r '' A. Let μ := Hⁿ⌞Q = μHE[n].restrict Q.

1. Blow-ups lie in V. Let r ∈ ℝ and a ∈ A. By hypothesis a − x ∈ V, and V is closed under scalar multiplication, so η_r(a) = r⁻¹ • (a − x) ∈ V. Hence S_r ⊆ V for every r ∈ ℝ.

2. Set-up of a contradiction. Let q ∈ Q and suppose q ∉ V. The subspace V of the finite-dimensional normed space ℝ^P is closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and nonempty (0 ∈ V). Hence d := infDist(q, V) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos).

3. A bump function. Define g : ℝ^P → ℝ by g(y) := max(0, d/2 − dist(y, q)).
 (i) g is continuous, as a max of continuous functions.
 (ii) g(y) ≥ 0 for every y.
 (iii) support g = ball(q, d/2), because max(0, t) ≠ 0 iff t > 0, and d/2 − dist(y, q) > 0 iff dist(y, q) < d/2.
 (iv) g has compact support. If y ∉ closedBall(q, d/2), then dist(y, q) > d/2, so g(y) = 0. Closed balls of ℝ^P are compact (HasCompactSupport.intro with isCompact_closedBall).
 Therefore g underlies an element f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), a CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ⟨⟨g, continuity⟩, compact support⟩, with f(y) = g(y) for all y.

4. g vanishes on V. Let v ∈ V. Then d = infDist(q, V) ≤ dist(q, v) = dist(v, q) (infDist_le_dist_of_mem). So d/2 − dist(v, q) ≤ −d/2 < 0, and g(v) = 0.

5. The blow-up integrals vanish. Fix r ∈ ℝ. Every point of S_r lies in V by step 1, and f = g vanishes on V by step 4, so f(y) = 0 for every y ∈ S_r. Hence ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
 No measurability of S_r is needed. The set O := {f ≠ 0} is open, hence Borel, and (Hⁿ⌞S_r)(O) = Hⁿ(O ∩ S_r) = Hⁿ(∅) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply for the measurable set O). So f = 0 holds Hⁿ⌞S_r-almost everywhere.

6. The limit plane integral is zero. Apply the second component of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q to f: the function r ↦ ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ tends to ∫_Q f dHⁿ along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. By step 5 this function is identically 0, so it also tends to 0 along 𝓝[>] 0. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial and ℝ is Hausdorff, so limits are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique). Hence ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0.

7. The plane measure charges every ball around q. The first component of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q gives finrank Q = n. Hence the support of μ = Hⁿ⌞Q equals Q (support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, SimonGMT Ch. 3, Rectifiable.lean). Since q ∈ Q, q lies in the support of μ, so every neighbourhood of q has positive μ-measure (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall). Because d/2 > 0, ball(q, d/2) is a neighbourhood of q, so μ(ball(q, d/2)) > 0.

8. Integrability. Since finrank Q = n, μ is a regular measure (regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), and in particular it is finite on compact sets. A continuous function with compact support is integrable for such a measure (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). So g is μ-integrable.

9. Positivity and contradiction. Since g ≥ 0 and g is μ-integrable, integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg gives 0 < ∫ g dμ ⟺ 0 < μ(support g). By step 3(iii) and step 7, μ(support g) = μ(ball(q, d/2)) > 0, so ∫ g dμ > 0. But the set integral ∫_Q f dHⁿ is by definition ∫ g dμ, and it is 0 by step 6. Contradiction.

10. Therefore every q ∈ Q lies in V, that is, Q ≤ V. The argument is uniform in n; for n = 0, Q = {0} ⊆ V in any case. ∎
key_steps: Every blow-up blowUpMap x r '' A = {r⁻¹(a − x) : a ∈ A} lies in V, because a − x ∈ V and V is a subspace.
If q ∈ Q \ V, then d := infDist(q, V) > 0. The bump g = max(0, d/2 − dist(·, q)) is in C_c, is nonnegative, has support ball(q, d/2), and vanishes on V.
Every blow-up integral of g is 0 (g vanishes pointwise on the blow-up; no measurability is needed). The approximate-tangent limit and uniqueness of limits along 𝓝[>] 0 give ∫_Q g dHⁿ = 0.
Since finrank Q = n, supp(Hⁿ⌞Q) = Q and Hⁿ⌞Q is regular. So g is integrable, μ(ball(q, d/2)) > 0, and integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg gives ∫_Q g dHⁿ > 0. This contradiction shows Q ≤ V.
